Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.domain.account

package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.domain.account
Account lifecycle: registration, e-mail verification, password change and reset.

SignedTokenService

Issues and verifies short-lived, signed, self-contained tokens (JWTs) that are bound to one purpose. The contract is deliberately independent of the account use cases so that other features can reuse it, for example the client assertions of a later issue:

  • issue(subject, purpose, ttl) returns a compact token whose subject, purpose and expiry are signed; the expiry is the issue instant plus ttl.
  • verify(token, purpose) returns the subject only when the signature, the issuer, the timestamps and the purpose all check out; for anything else (expired, tampered, wrong purpose, malformed) it returns an empty optional and never throws, and it never reveals which check failed.
  • A token proves a claim but is not single-use: anything that must be consumed once uses an AccountTokenRepository instead.

AccountMailer

Sends the transactional e-mails of the account lifecycle. The messages are plain text and the implementation chooses the wording and the language, never the platform's default locale. A delivery failure is reported as an AccountMailException (never the mail framework's own type, and never with the address or the token in it), so that the calling use case's transaction rolls back and nothing is left stored for a message that was never delivered. The callers keep their answer independent of whether an address is registered: every registration path sends a message, and the reset-request endpoint answers the same even when its message cannot be delivered. The methods receive the raw token or the link material the message must contain and never a password.
